scenario: [LGRA.22.4]: a library-qualified schema reference is `p.NAME`, and in a type position "every `.` in a schema reference separates the library path from the schema". Library `plant.zone` declares `Trig`, `Alert` and `Mark`. A pattern head `plant.zone.Trig t`, `emit plant.zone.Alert logical` and `publish plant.zone.Mark` (a `publish` takes no modifier, [LTIE.4.9]): a two-segment path, schema last. Pinned as `dsc_term_order` so both rules have to LOWER, not only parse: a compiler that split the path anywhere but before the last name finds no schema and leaves the rule unlowered. PATH PINNED: `dsc.parse`'s `lgra_8_1_take_type_ref` (`tr_qualified`), resolved by `dsc.resolve`'s `lgra_22_4_pattern_head` and `dsc.rete`'s `action_schema`.
rules_ds:
import plant.zone

rule raise_both:
    plant.zone.Trig t
->
    emit plant.zone.Alert logical v: t.v
    publish plant.zone.Mark v: t.v

rule on_alert:
    plant.zone.Alert a
->
    log info "alert {a.v}"

libraries.plant.zone:
schema Trig scope logical:
    v: Int key

schema Alert scope logical:
    v: Int key

schema Mark scope logical:
    v: Int key
